title: Diagnostic assessment (form A)
description: Baseline and reassessment instrument. Moved from the browser (frontend/src/data/assessmentData.ts) to the server in T1.5 so it is scored server-side and the answer key never reaches the client. Ten items over four domains: below the three-items-per-competency threshold for every competency, so it gives domain-level evidence only.

questions.prompt: What is the primary objective of data confidentiality in information security?
options: Ensuring data cannot be modified by unauthorized users
Ensuring data is accessible only to authorized individuals
Ensuring systems remain continuously operational without interruption
Ensuring senders cannot deny transmitting a message
questions.explanation: Confidentiality ensures that sensitive information is accessible only to authorized users and protected from unauthorized disclosure.

questions.prompt: Which cryptographic mechanism provides a one-way mathematical transformation to verify data integrity?
questions.explanation: Cryptographic hash functions produce a fixed-size digest from input data; any modification to the original data alters the digest.

questions.prompt: Which cryptographic method uses a mathematically linked pair of public and private keys?
questions.explanation: Asymmetric cryptography uses a public key for encryption/verification and a mathematically paired private key for decryption/signing.

questions.prompt: What is the primary role of the Diffie-Hellman protocol in secure communications?
options: Securely establishing a shared symmetric key over an untrusted channel
Scanning network packets for signature anomalies
Storing encrypted credentials in hardware security modules
questions.explanation: Diffie-Hellman allows two parties to agree on a shared secret over an insecure channel without transmitting the secret itself.

questions.prompt: What two critical security properties are established when an entity signs data with their private key?
questions.explanation: Digital signatures verify the sender identity (authentication) and prove the origin of the message (non-repudiation).

questions.prompt: Why does Shor's quantum algorithm pose a catastrophic threat to classical RSA and ECC algorithms?
options: It brute-forces AES-256 keys in constant time
It efficiently solves integer factorization and discrete logarithms in polynomial time
It disables firewall routing rules across the internet
It intercepts optical fiber signals without physical access
questions.explanation: Shor's algorithm solves prime factorization (underpinning RSA) and discrete log problems (underpinning ECC) exponentially faster than classical computers.

questions.prompt: What is the "Harvest Now, Decrypt Later" (HNDL) cybersecurity threat model?
options: Malware extracting private keys from browser cache files
Adversaries intercepting and storing encrypted traffic today to decrypt with future quantum computers
Automated scraping of public GitHub repositories for hardcoded API keys
questions.explanation: In HNDL attacks, adversaries capture and archive encrypted communications today, anticipating future cryptanalytically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs) to decrypt them.

questions.prompt: Which mathematical framework serves as the primary foundation for modern NIST post-quantum standards (such as ML-KEM and ML-DSA)?
questions.explanation: Lattice-based cryptography, particularly the Learning With Errors (LWE / Module-LWE) problem, provides hardness against both classical and quantum attacks.

questions.prompt: Which NIST Post-Quantum Cryptographic standard represents the standardized Module-Lattice Key Encapsulation Mechanism (formerly CRYSTALS-Kyber)?
questions.explanation: FIPS 203 defines ML-KEM (Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism), the primary quantum-resistant standard for general encryption and key exchange.

questions.prompt: What is the recommended transitional strategy for migrating enterprise TLS protocols to post-quantum security?
options: Immediately deprecating all symmetric AES ciphers
Deploying hybrid key exchange combining classical algorithms (e.g., X25519) with PQC algorithms (e.g., ML-KEM-768)
Switching all web traffic to plain unencrypted HTTP
questions.explanation: Hybrid key exchange pairs classical algorithms with post-quantum algorithms, ensuring security is maintained even if one algorithm experiences an unforeseen weakness.
